text:
maria: Heads-up, ran a quantized rerank bring-up and saw ndcg@10 drop ~3% vs fp16 on the new candidate harvest. Might be formatting-related, asking for eyes.
leo: hmm, which dataset / candidate recipe?
maria: small subsample from webqa_v2 (10k queries). candidates are scraped passages, some include raw HTML and markdown. fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.482, int8-ptq -> 0.468. MRR also down a bit.
leo: that delta is borderline but worrying. do you have the eval command?
maria: yep, calling the harness:
```
python -m eval.rerank --model rerank-v2-fp16 --candidates candidates_v2.jsonl --queries queries_subset.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42
python -m eval.rerank --model rerank-v2-int8 --candidates candidates_v2.jsonl --queries queries_subset.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42
```
maria: same seed, same split. no other changes.
dan: could be tokenizer differences after quant conversion? unlikely but check whitespace handling and truncation. also check candidate sort order (we sometimes shuffle during preprocess).
julia: also try stripping html/markdown. i've seen rerankers react badly when markup changes the tokenization distribution.
maria: good call. i'm running a small probe: strip html + normalize whitespace. will post numbers.
(eval-bot): job 52172 finished: fp16 on subset -> ndcg@10=0.482, mrr=0.367; int8 baseline -> ndcg@10=0.468, mrr=0.360
maria: probe 1 (strip-html + collapse whitespace): int8 -> ndcg@10=0.479, mrr=0.365
leo: whoa, that pushes int8 almost to fp16. suggests markup was amplifying quantization sensitivity.
dan: nice. can you diff token counts per document before/after strip? maybe markup creates weird subtokenization.
maria: quick counts: median tokens per doc before=312, after=298. some docs drop a lot (code blocks and tables).
julia: that explains it. quant kernels are sensitive to sequence length distribution and KV packing boundaries. smaller sequences -> different batching behavior -> slight scoring shifts.
leo: action item: add a preprocessing rule for candidate pipeline to strip noisy markup for rerank training/serve. also add an eval variant that keeps raw markup so we monitor regressions.
dan: we should also re-run with a different seed and slightly larger sample to check significance. 3% over 10k queries might be noisy.
maria: on it. launching 50k-sample runs with seeds [42, 101, 7]. will report.
(eval-bot): job 52199 queued: int8 + strip-html on 50k sample (seeds 42,101,7). estimated 2h.
leo: nice catch. can you add a short note in the onboarding doc about candidate text canonicalization? saved us time. :thumbsup:
maria: will add to the model bring-up checklist under "text normalization" and link to the preproc script: https://internal.gist/normalize-candidates.py
julia: also mention that candidate ordering must be deterministic between fp16 and int8 eval runs. we found shuffle hooks that differ by default.
dan: agree. final ask: add a quick AB eval comparing fp16 vs int8 on the full validation holdout with the new preproc. if metrics converge we can proceed with canary.
maria: noted. will follow up when 50k runs finish. thanks all.
